sections.title: Basic Concept of Phrasal Verbs
sections.content: A phrasal verb is formed by combining a verb with a particle (a preposition or an adverb). For example: look + after = look after. The meaning of a phrasal verb can be different from the meaning of the main verb alone. Example: 'look after' means 'to take care of'.

sections.title: Direct Meaning Identification
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the phrasal verb (verb + particle). Step 2: Recall its common meaning or usage. Step 3: Choose the option that gives the most accurate meaning. Example: Give up → Quit or stop trying.

sections.title: Fill in the Blanks (Correct Particle)
sections.content: Step 1: Understand the meaning of the sentence. Step 2: Determine which particle (up, off, on, out, etc.) completes the meaning. Step 3: Match it with common phrasal verb patterns. Example: She looked after the child. (look after = take care)

sections.title: Replacing a Standard Verb with a Phrasal Verb
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the meaning of the given verb. Step 2: Think of a common phrasal verb with the same meaning. Step 3: Place it correctly in the sentence. Example: Continue → Carry on.

sections.title: Common Phrasal Verb Patterns
sections.content: Some phrasal verbs are very common, such as: give up (stop), find out (discover), put off (delay), look for (search). Practicing these helps in recognizing them quickly.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Changing the particle changes the meaning. 2. Assuming the literal meaning of the verb. 3. Using the wrong preposition or particle.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: A phrasal verb consists of a verb plus a particle. Its meaning is often different from the main verb alone. Regular practice helps in quickly recognizing and understanding common phrasal verbs.

tricks.title: Identify Verb + Particle
tricks.explanation: First check which small word follows the verb.

tricks.title: Common Meaning Memory
tricks.explanation: Some phrasal verbs appear very frequently, so memorize them.

tricks.title: Sentence Meaning Check
tricks.explanation: Understand the full sentence before filling the blank.

tricks.title: Particle Change = Meaning Change
tricks.explanation: Changing the particle can completely change the meaning.
tricks.example: Look for = search, Look after = take care.

tricks.title: Single Verb Replacement
tricks.explanation: Some single verbs have equivalent phrasal verbs.

tricks.title: Daily Use Trick
tricks.explanation: Learn phrasal verbs that are commonly used in everyday language.

tricks.title: Context Guess Trick
tricks.explanation: If you do not remember the meaning, guess it from the context of the sentence.

tricks.title: Two Word Memory Trick
tricks.explanation: Always memorize phrasal verbs as two-word combinations.
